correctness.rationale: The pinned RESULT.md specifies n>=3, t>0, equal diagonal conductance, ordinary degree and only one-vertex marginals. Root-edge marking in the weighted Matrix–Tree cofactor gives Z_n(t;z)=(n−1+t)z[d+(n−1+t)z]^(n−2)(n−2+t+tz), d=n²−3n+1+(2n−1)t. At z=1, d+n−1+t=n(n−2+2t), so the pgf factors with p=(n−1+t)/[n(n−2+2t)] and q=t/(n−2+2t). A derivative in t of the convex expectation equals −(n−2)(n−1)(t−1)EΔ²φ(1+Bin(n−3,p))/[n(n−2+2t)^3]; strict for strictly convex φ and for the leaf-test φ(j)=(2−j)+ since p<1. Its moment deficit equals (n−2)(n−1)(t−1)²/[n²(n−2+2t)²]. Binomial pgf convergence at t_n/n→c∈[0,∞], including ∞, proves the independent limit and 2u e^(−u) leaves. Independently recomputed nine rational weighted-Laplacian cofactors against factorization, at multiple n,t,z. Finite checks corroborate but do not extend the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: A one-parameter matching perturbation of an extremely symmetric graph has a sharp, nontrivial convex-order and leaf-count extremum at uniform conductance; the order-n conductance window produces a distinctive non-Poisson degree law even with fixed mean. These are natural graph-probability features, not an arbitrary tiny numerical check, and can support weighted tree asymptotic studies.

final_claim: For every n>=3 and t>0, one marked vertex of the matching-weighted K_n,n Gibbs spanning tree has degree 1+Bin(n−2,p(n,t))+Bernoulli(q(n,t)) independently; the law is uniquely convex-order-maximal at t=1, expected leaves uniquely maximize there, and t_n/n→c yields an explicit Poisson–Bernoulli crossover and leaf-density limit.
limitations: Only common conductance along one perfect matching, not arbitrary inhomogeneous edge weights.
Only vertex degree marginal and expected leaves, no joint correlations or convergence rates.
